title: Provisional quota reservations and ledger reconciliation for offline collectors
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped or intermittent-connectivity environments can generate requests while the on-prem collector cannot immediately sync usage to the central billing ledger. This creates two related correctness problems: (1) local rate-limiting and quota enforcement must still prevent over-commit while offline, and (2) when usage bundles are submitted later, we must reconcile them into the global ledger without double-counting or unfairly denying capacity.

Proposed solution: implement a local provisional quota reservation ledger on the on-prem collector that issues short-lived reservations (provisional tokens) for requests while offline, combined with a deterministic reconciliation protocol when the collector reconnects. Key components:
- Provisional reservation API (local-only): lightweight incrementing reservations with expiry and optional preemption. Reservations decrement local available quota and are included in the offline bundle metadata.
- Monotonic reservation sequence numbers: every reservation and usage record includes a collector-scoped monotonic sequence and per-instance UUID to enable idempotent ingestion and ordering on the central ledger.
- Compact signed manifests: when uplinking, collectors send compressed bundles plus a signed manifest that summarizes reservations, final usage, and tombstones for cancelled reservations. Central reconciler validates signatures, sequence ranges, and checks for gaps.
- Merge semantics and conflict resolution: the central ledger applies a three-phase reconciliation: validate, tentatively apply (reserve on global ledger), then finalize once bundle consistency checks pass. Conflicting reservations (same customer, overlapping time) are resolved by earliest-sequence wins with configurable slack windows.
- Local enforcement fallbacks: configurable policy for on-prem behavior when provisional quota exhausted (hard block, best-effort degrade, burst with debt). Default policy: conservative block to preserve global accounting correctness.
- Observability and audits: per-collector reconciliation reports, discrepancy metrics (reserved vs final), and an admin tool to replay bundles for manual correction.

Deliverables:
- Collector prototype changes (Go): local reservation store, sequence allocator, manifest signer.
- Central reconciler service updates: bundle validator, conflict resolver, audit trail persister.
- API/Config: local policy flags, global reconciliation window, and admin endpoints to inspect pending/unapplied bundles.
- Test harness: end-to-end simulation of network partitions, clock skew, duplicate-bundle ingestion, and heavy parallel reservations.

Acceptance criteria:
- No more than 0.1% of reconciled bundles require manual intervention in 10K simulated collectors workload.
- Central ledger idempotency guarantees: applying the same bundle twice changes nothing after first apply.
- Reconciliation latency under normal reconnect conditions <= 30s for validation stage, <= 5m for finalize with large bundles.
- Customers with default conservative policy never see quota violations (global over-commit).

References:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Private+Offline+Quota+Draft
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/1489

Risks & trade-offs:
- Conservatively blocking on-prem requests may impact customer UX during long outages; we provide policy knobs (allow-debt) for those willing to accept risk.
- Complexity increase in central reconciler and need for robust signing/verification to prevent tampering.
- Clock skew and partial bundles require careful watermarking and gap-detection heuristics.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement prototype behind feature flag and run Canary on staging Private clusters.
2) Run integration tests with synthetic traffic and simulated partitions.
3) Beta with 3 customers that opt into the feature and accept default conservative policy.
4) Full rollout with monitoring and automated rollback on >0.5% manual reconciliation rate.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence. Decided to prioritize conservative default (block) for correctness. Action: Diego to prototype reservation store.

2026-02-25 - Diego Morales: Initial prototype: local reservation store using SQLite with WAL mode. Sequence allocator implemented as per-collector monotonic counter. Pushed prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector/tree/feat/provisional-reservations
2026-03-02 - Priya Shah (PM) review: Concern about UX for long outages. Requested metrics to surface number of blocked requests and optional 'allow-debt' policy with debt windows. Added to scope.
2026-03-05 - Security review scheduled: need to ensure manifest signing uses customer KMS key for Private deployments. Security owners: Marco Ruiz. TODO: threat model for replay attacks.

2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Reconciler design doc draft uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/reconciler-draft. Implemented tentative-apply + finalize phases in central reconciler prototype. Edge case: overlapping reservations from multiple collectors for same API key when network partitioned between collectors. Proposed tie-breaker: earliest sequence wins + configurable slack of 2 seconds.
2026-03-10 - Design feedback from Elena Park (SRE): Recommend adding bundle checksum and per-file manifests to speed partial recovery and to enable parallel validation of large bundles.

2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Integration tests passing locally for duplicate-bundle idempotency and sequence gap detection. Next: run end-to-end test harness with 500 simulated collectors and 48h of synthetic traffic. PR queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/221
